package_info.package_versions: 2.3.5–2.3.31, 2.5–2.5.10 (vulnerable versions exploited in 2017 Equifax breach and other incidents)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contained a critical, unpatched remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2017-5638) in certain versions. Attackers exploited this flaw by sending specially crafted HTTP requests to vulnerable endpoints, allowing them to execute arbitrary commands on affected servers. This vulnerability was the entry point for the Equifax breach and several other high-profile attacks, highlighting the severe risk of using outdated or unpatched open source components in production environments.

execution_context.trigger: HTTP request processing (when a vulnerable endpoint receives a crafted Content-Type header)
execution_context.file_location: org.apache.struts2.dispatcher.multipart.JakartaMultiPartRequest (Jakarta Multipart parser in Struts core framework)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
String contentType = request.getHeader("Content-Type");
Object value = Ognl.getValue(contentType, context, root);
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Processes the Content-Type header from incoming HTTP requests using OGNL expression evaluation. If the header contains a malicious OGNL payload, it is evaluated as code, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary commands on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Evaluating user-controlled HTTP headers as OGNL expressions is highly dangerous and enables attackers to inject and execute arbitrary code remotely. This behavior directly leads to remote code execution vulnerabilities.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal application code should treat HTTP headers as data and never evaluate them as code. Secure implementations sanitize or strictly validate input before any processing. Here, the code evaluates unsanitized input, violating secure coding practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: OGNL is legitimately used in Struts for dynamic expression evaluation, but only with trusted, internally generated data. Evaluating untrusted user input, especially HTTP headers, is never legitimate and is a critical security flaw.
key_indicators: Direct use of user-supplied HTTP headers in OGNL expression evaluation
Absence of input sanitization or validation before code execution
OGNL.getValue or similar dynamic evaluation functions used on request data

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request with a malicious Content-Type header to a vulnerable Struts endpoint.
attack_chain.leads_to: OGNL expression in the Content-Type header is evaluated by the server, enabling remote code execution.

attack_chain.action: Malicious OGNL payload executes with the permissions of the web server process, allowing the attacker to run arbitrary system commands, exfiltrate data, or move laterally within the network.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full system compromise, data theft, installation of further malware, or use of the server as a pivot point for additional attacks.

behavioral_signatures: OGNL or similar expression evaluation functions invoked with user-supplied HTTP header values
Unexpected child process creation (e.g., shell, cmd.exe) by the web application process after HTTP requests
Unusual outbound network connections initiated by the web server process following HTTP requests to Struts endpoints
file_indicators: Presence of org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/multipart/JakartaMultiPartRequest.class from vulnerable Struts versions
Struts core JAR files with version numbers 2.3.5–2.3.31 or 2.5–2.5.10
Application dependency manifests (pom.xml) referencing vulnerable Struts versions
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests to Struts endpoints with suspicious Content-Type headers containing OGNL payload patterns (e.g., %{...})
Outbound connections to attacker-controlled IPs or domains immediately after such requests
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor HTTP traffic for requests to Struts endpoints with Content-Type headers containing OGNL expressions (e.g., %{...}). Scan application dependencies and deployed JARs for known vulnerable Struts versions. Detect unexpected process creation or outbound network activity from the web server process following suspicious requests. Deploy WAF rules to block known OGNL injection patterns and enforce automated dependency management to prevent use of vulnerable Struts versions.
